Out of the 4 internal configurations this case is designed for, this one is the most ambitious. It fits a 240mm AIO cooler, full-size GPU, SFX PSU, ITX motherboard, and 2 hard drives all in about 10L of space.

To make sure the cooling is acceptable with all these components crammed into this tiny amount of space, I have conducted a thorough temperature test with this configuration (details here). Compared to an optimal, open-cooling configuration, the !nverse case performed only 8 deg worse for an overclocked i5 (4.4GHz) and 5 deg worse for the R9 390. These are differences in max temperatures while running Prime95 and Unigine Valley.

The next prototype will probably be the one that will be sent to reviewers. Crowdfunding should come after that.

90th anniversary of the first television demonstration by John Logie Baird

If you hadn't noticed Google's doodle yet, today is the 90th anniversary of the first public television demonstration by John Logie Baird in 1926. A lot of people credit Philo Farnsworth for the invention of TV but that isn't correct. Mechanical systems were sold and broadcasts were on the air quite a few years before electronic TV was invented. It is rare to see Baird get any real credit.
